title: Immune-System Negative Selection for Anomaly Detection on Agent Activations

original_idea.body:
# Immune-System Negative Selection for Anomaly Detection on Agent Activations

**Problem:** Supervised monitors need labeled sabotage examples, which are scarce. We want to flag never-before-seen anomalous behavior using only normal examples.

**Direction:** Import the artificial immune system negative-selection algorithm. Collect activations on benign trajectories ('self'), train a one-class detector for 'non-self', and test whether it flags held-out sabotage, comparing to a supervised probe. Small open-weight model.

**Why it matters:** Targets detection of novel dangerous behaviors using only benign data. Activation extraction + one-class model fits a consumer GPU, no training from scratch.

**Relevant context:** Negative selection (Forrest); SycophantSee (Apart hackathon).
